Comment on Proposed Rule: Reproductive Health Services 
RIN 2900-AS31 (VA) 
September 3, 2025 
 
The American Association of Pro-Life Obstetricians and Gynecologists (AAPLOG) is the 
largest non-sectarian pro-life medical professional organization in the world, representing 
approximately 8,000 women’s healthcare professionals. We were founded to represent the 
vast majority of OB/GYNs who do not perform induced abortion, which intends the death of 
our fetal patients. We recognize based on the medical evidence that this practice is not 
healthcare, and we are passionate about providing excellent, evidence-based healthcare 
to ALL our patients. Our members include many physicians who are veterans and many 
who actively serve at VA hospitals. Thus, the Proposed Reproductive Health Services Rule 
directly affects our membership.  
 
AAPLOG fully supports reinstating the full exclusion on induced abortions and abortion 
counseling from the medical benefits package, as was the status prior to 2022. We 
appreciate the removal of the radical pro-abortion political agenda that was forced on VA 
healthcare employees to participate in induced abortion, forcing medical professionals to 
kill human beings in utero and act against their consciences.   
 
Pregnancy is not a disease; it is a natural physiological process. Between 76-93% of 
OB/GYNs do no perform abortions.i Induced abortion is not healthcare as it does not treat a 
disease process, always ends the life of one of our patients, and often causes significant 
mental or physical harm to our other patient.  
 
Before the prior Administration’s unethical and deadly changes, the medical benefits to VA 
and CHAMPVA as far as abortion was concerned only incorporated conditions where the 
life of the mother was in danger. These circumstances do indeed constitute medical 
emergencies which sadly can be experienced by our nation’s heroes and their families. 
When a mother is facing a life-threatening condition during pregnancy, a maternal fetal 
separation procedure to end her pregnancy would already be covered under the proposed 
rule. AAPLOG strongly encourages, in reinstating the rule, to keep this as the only 
circumstance in which pregnancy termination is covered. Women who suffer the violence 
of sexual assault need and deserve the best help and care possible that is evidence-based 
to be beneficial to her. That does not include induced abortion.   
 
There are well-established maternal health morbidities associated with induced abortion, 
including preterm birth in subsequent pregnancies and an increase in mental health 
disorders.ii Induced abortion causes a 7x increased risk for suicide, as well as an increased 
risk of drug abuse and major depression requiring hospitalization compared with birth.iii  

 
2 
 
 
 
This risk is especially high in women with pre-existing mental health disorders, including 
post-traumatic stress disorder.    
 
The trauma of sexual assault should not be exacerbated with the trauma of induced 
abortion. Women deserve better treatment than adding one violent act onto another, 
especially subsidized by American tax dollars. Instead, our resources should be invested 
in ensuring that our active-duty military, veterans, and their family have the mental health 
counseling and support they need.  
 
Induced abortion also robs women of the health benefits of pregnancy – both physical and 
mental. Pregnancy represents a normal functioning of women’s bodies, and there are a 
multitude of benefits of pregnancy for women. Research has shown that women with 
children have significantly lower rates of depressioniv and increased happinessv compared 
to women without children. Pregnancy also decreases a woman’s risk of several cancers, 
including breastvi, uterinevii, and ovarian.viii Additionally, women with children have a longer 
lifespanix whereas induced abortion has been shown in large registry-based studies to 
cause a higher mortality risk than either no pregnancy or full-term births.x  
 
Inherent in what is covered within VA and CHAMPVA medical benefits is a stamp of 
approval on what is necessary and most beneficial for the health and well-being of women 
and their families. While sadly medical emergencies that threaten a mother’s life do occur 
and their treatment should be included here, induced abortion should not. It is not an 
essential part of women’s healthcare, as evidenced by the fact that the vast majority of 
OB/GYNs do not perform induced abortions, and it is not beneficial for women, as 
highlighted throughout this comment. All women deserve excellent, evidence-based 
healthcare.   
  
AAPLOG supports the proposed rule and thanks the VA for this reinstatement of the pre-
Biden medical benefits package regarding induced abortion.   
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Dr. Christina Francis 
CEO 
American Association of Pro-Life Obstetricians and Gynecologists (AAPLOG)
